### Later-chunk control at `fc1c8e6f`

Added a test-only later-chunk mutation after synchronized readback verifies both earlier converted frame pixels and the accumulated sum. A first-chunk-only mutant must fail the same acceptance predicate while completing nvCOMP decoding and matching original-reference MRC/STAR products. Fixed rows require compact fallback and complete product identity. Production sources and trusted-input policy are unchanged.

Local configure/build and four focused CTests PASS, including 18 fake-CUDA host controls; independent Sol review found no material issue and independently rebuilt all 18 host controls. See `docs/issue215/later-chunk.md` for commands and source/evidence limits. [Current-head Linux CI](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/actions/runs/39773679138) **PASS**: CPU build/checks and CUDA compile-only. The new nvCOMP instrumented targets are not built by this CI configuration; their CUDA compilation and native discrimination remain UNRUN. CUDA compilation of the new instrumented targets, native later-chunk fallback and native mutant discrimination remain **UNRUN**; retained historical native evidence is not requalified.

---

Fixes #215. Pin the tag-scan TIFF descriptor's device, inode, size and nanosecond mtime; check every fresh reader and recheck the path/handles before chunk submission. Identity changes decline into the existing host reader with a named log witness. D1's trusted immutable-input precondition, routes, dependencies and numerical gates are unchanged.

Evidence at code/test head `76fa8112` (PR head `bbca3838` adds documentation/evidence only):
- All six append/atomic-rename mutations are observed: the controls fail with the production fix reversed and pass with it; the fixed nine-row run passes completely.
- Release full CTest: CPU **74/74** on cpu64; CUDA **108/108** on 4GPUs; CUDA+nvCOMP **111/112**, with only the two import-subset `TimeoutExpired` errors attributed to independent #246. Compiler occupancy is retained; every other test, including the new CTest, passes. No test limit was changed.
- On 4GPUs, both real tutorial TIFFs keep the auto `nvcomp` route in G/L. All MRC/STAR products match unfixed auto and fixed compact, with only declared path/timestamp normalization.

[Commands, revisions, input/binary hashes, route logs and raw evidence](https://github.com/KingAlejandro/MotionCorr-standalone/blob/bbca3838/docs/issue215/README.md). SUPPORT §8 and the post-RC0 acceptance report are updated. Performance, the full QF campaign, other corpus families, multi-GPU scaling/publication, SCARF and Tier D science were not rerun.

Next action: review the identity guard and discriminating/native evidence; #246 is a separate test-harness fix. No maintainer output-parity decision is needed for this fix. Do not merge.

reviews.body:
Source and retained-evidence review at bbca3838; no new native run performed. I found no blocking correctness issue in the identity guard. Pinning the tag-scan descriptor avoids a separate stat/open race, and checking both the pathname and reader descriptors catches replacement while an old inode remains open. The new post-upload early returns also reach ScratchScope/endIngestScratch, which drains both streams before the host fallback can reuse the Fourier arena or pinned staging.

One useful nonblocking control to add: mutate on a later chunk, after an earlier chunk has actually been converted into d_Iframes/d_Isum. The current tag-close, reader-open and first strip-read mutations all precede the first decode; a regression that checks identity only on the first chunk could therefore still pass all six rows. With the existing two-frame chunk setting, a delayed mutation plus a witness of earlier conversion would test that partial nvCOMP accumulation is discarded and the complete compact result matches the host reference.

The retained fixed/reversed controls discriminate the identity guard rather than merely accepting any fallback, and the G/L tutorial comparisons support the bounded healthy-path invariance claim. The documented immutable-input precondition and lack of arbitrary corrupt-Deflate protection remain important.

title: Fix #215: pin TIFF identity across nvCOMP ingest
